property_summary: Only the owner can successfully withdraw; calls from non-owners must revert.
When withdrawAll is called, it reverts for non-owners and does not succeed for callers that are not the owner (i.e., only owner calls can succeed).

If withdrawAll call does not revert then the caller-specified _recipient must be the beneficiary who receives the contract's balance (so the caller's provided recipient address should end up owning any Ether transferred).
After owner withdrawAll(recipient) the recipient receives the entire contract balance (address(c).balance becomes 0 and recipient balance increases by that full amount).
If withdrawAll is called by the owner, the call must revert (i.e., non-owner works) — owner-only requirement enforces caller equality with c.owner().
When withdrawAll is called by any account, the call either reverts or (if it succeeds) drains the contract completely so address(c).balance == 0 afterwards.
After the owner invokes withdrawAll with a recipient, the contract's balance becomes zero (all funds forwarded to recipient).
Calling withdrawAll by the owner must not revert (i.e., succeeds) for any recipient when invoked by the contract owner.
When withdrawAll is called by the owner, the call succeeds (does not revert) exactly when the recipient is a non-zero address.
When the owner calls withdrawAll, the call must NOT revert and contract balance must become zero afterwards (funds forwarded).
When withdrawAll is called by the owner it must not revert (i.e., the call completes) for any recipient address.

For any caller who is the owner and for any positive ETH balance held by the contract, calling withdrawAll(recipient) always forwards the contract's entire balance to the given recipient (so address(c).balance becomes zero); the mutant that removes the transfer can leave the contract balance nonzero and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For any caller who is the owner and any positive contract balance, calling withdrawAll(recipient) always reduces address(c).balance to zero (the reference transfers the full balance; the mutant that removed the transfer can leave the balance nonzero).

If the caller is owner, then after calling withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's balance is transferred to the recipient (so recipient's balance increases by the contract's pre-call balance); the mutant that removes the transfer can leave the recipient's balance unchanged for some inputs.

For any owner caller and any positive contract balance, calling withdrawAll(recipient) succeeds (does not revert) and returns (does not revert) while preserving that the contract's balance becomes zero (the reference transfers out funds; the mutant that removed the transfer still returns but leaves balance nonzero) — we assert the call succeeds and that address(c).balance == 0 after the call; the buggy version can leave balance nonzero causing the assertion to fail for some fuzzed inputs.
Only the owner can cause the contract to send its entire balance out (calls by non-owner must not withdraw the contract balance).

property_summary: Calling withdrawAll by a non-owner always reverts (i.e., only the owner can successfully call withdrawAll).
If the provided caller equals c.owner() then calling withdrawAll should succeed, and if it does not equal c.owner() then calling withdrawAll should revert.
The provided caller equals the contract's recorded owner exactly when the attempted withdrawAll call does not revert.
The provided caller equals the contract's recorded owner exactly when the attempted withdrawAll call does not revert.

For any recipient contract whose payable fallback/receive reverts, the correct contract using transfer will always revert (leaving c.balance unchanged) when owner calls withdrawAll, while the mutant using call may succeed or behave differently; thus reference always preserves contract balance on such failing recipients but mutant can change it.

For any recipient contract that intentionally reverts on receiving Ether, the correct contract (using transfer) preserves its balance (withdrawAll call reverts) for every input owner/recipient/amount, whereas the mutant (using call) can succeed in sending funds (changing c.balance) when the recipient's fallback does not revert or when it intentionally accepts, so the invariant that c.balance remains unchanged for a reverting recipient is broken by the mutant.

If the recipient's fallback reverts, then withdrawAll called by the owner must leave the contract balance unchanged (call must revert or fail to transfer) — the mutant using low-level call can succeed or behave differently, breaking this rule for some recipient behaviors.

For any recipient that always reverts on receiving ether, the correct contract (using transfer) will revert and therefore preserve C's balance when the owner calls withdrawAll; the mutant (using low-level call) can observe the recipient's non-reverting behavior and may succeed, changing C's balance, so the invariant that address(c).balance remains unchanged for a reverting recipient is violated by the mutant for some inputs.
